candidate.answerReason: Equal jar volumes give alcohol shares p/(p+1) and q/(q+1), and water shares 1/(p+1) and 1/(q+1). Dividing the total alcohol by the total water gives choice E.

methods.label: Add alcohol and water separately
methods.explanation:
The identical full jars contain equal volumes. Measure volume in jarfuls, so each jar contains \(1\) unit; choosing this common unit leaves the final ratio unchanged.

A ratio \(p:1\) divides the first jar into \(p+1\) shares, giving alcohol volume \(p/(p+1)\) and water volume \(1/(p+1)\). The second jar similarly contributes \(q/(q+1)\) alcohol and \(1/(q+1)\) water. Thus the total alcohol volume \(A\) and water volume \(W\) are
\[
A=\frac{p}{p+1}+\frac{q}{q+1},
\qquad
W=\frac1{p+1}+\frac1{q+1}.
\]
Since \(p\) and \(q\) are volume ratios, they are nonnegative. Hence \(p+1\) and \(q+1\) are positive, and \(W>0\). Multiplying the numerator and denominator of \(A/W\) by \((p+1)(q+1)\) gives
\[
\frac{A}{W}
=\frac{p(q+1)+q(p+1)}{(q+1)+(p+1)}
=\frac{p+q+2pq}{p+q+2}.
\]
The final denominator is positive as well. The answer is \(\frac{p+q+2pq}{p+q+2}\), choice E.
